symptoms: The failure names a missing output location for a shuffle
It appears on the stage that READS the shuffle, and the stage that wrote it had reported success
The whole map stage is recomputed after the failure
likely_causes: The executor that held the shuffle output is gone, and the block it wrote went with it
The external shuffle service is not in use, so shuffle output does not survive the executor that produced it
Dynamic allocation removed the executor after the map stage finished and before the reduce stage read it
diagnostic_steps: Read the shuffle bytes the stage wrote: this failure costs the recomputation of the whole map stage, and the size of it is what the cost is proportional to
Read whether executors were lost between the map stage and the reduce stage -- the two events together tell one story that neither tells alone
Separate it from a fetch failure of a single block: a missing output LOCATION is the whole executor, not one connection
fixes: Reduce the shuffle so less has to be recomputed when a loss happens
Keep the executor alive across the two stages when dynamic allocation is removing it too eagerly
Treat the executor loss itself when there is one, because this exception is its consequence
unsafe_fixes: Raising retries to get past it: the map stage is recomputed on every retry, and the cost multiplies
Disabling dynamic allocation without measuring, which pays for idle capacity for the whole run
verification: Re-run and confirm the reduce stage completes without recomputing the map stage. Shuffle bytes written, before and after, over the same input
rollback: Revert the allocation or shuffle change. No data axis is required when the change is of capacity, and declaring that is part of the verification
